intro: Read a short, fictional news report and tell its main facts from the headline.
p.ampliar.consejo: You can extend a timetable or a house. Its future is regular: «ampliará».
p.biblioteca.consejo: It is not «librería»: a librería sells books and a biblioteca lends them.
p.barrio.consejo: The «rr» rolls strongly: «BA-rryo». It is the area where your neighbours live.
p.préstamo.consejo: It has an accent on the e: «PRES-ta-mo». A book loan: you take it and give it back.
p.vecinos.consejo: They live in your building or neighbourhood. Singular: «vecino»; feminine: «vecina».
p.horario.consejo: A library has a horario: it opens at some hours and closes at others.
p.noticia.consejo: A noticia tells something that has happened. The plural is «noticias».
p.entre semana.consejo: You say «entre semana», without an article. It is the opposite of the weekend.
p.titular.consejo: As a noun it is «el titular». It goes above the news item and gives the main idea.
p.a partir de.consejo: It marks the start of a change: «a partir del lunes». «De + el» joins as «del».
p.cerrar.consejo: It changes e to ie: «cierro», «cierra». Its opposite is «abrir».
p.más tarde.consejo: «Dos horas más tarde» compares two times. The opposite is «más temprano».
b1.texto:
In a short news item, the first sentence and the time and place expressions tell you **what happens**, **when** and **where**.

Then check the details: **who** is affected, **when** a change begins and whether the text gives a **reason**.

News talks about things that will happen using the **future**: **ampliará**, **cerrará**, **abrirá**. It also uses **a partir de** (from when) and **más tarde que** (comparing times).

The news item in this lesson is invented and is used for language practice.
b2.f0.texto: Have you read the news about the library?
b2.f2.texto: The library extends its opening hours.
b2.f5.texto: Until what time will it be open?
b2.f6.texto: It will close at eight in the evening.
b2.f7.texto: It is good news for the neighbourhood.
b4.texto:
The future of regular verbs adds the endings to the **whole infinitive**:

- **-é**, **-ás**, **-á**, **-emos**, **-éis**, **-án**.
- **ampliar** → **ampliará**; **cerrar** → **cerrará**; **abrir** → **abrirá**.

With **él / ella / ellos** news uses **-á** and **-án**: **abrirá** (one), **abrirán** (several).

**A partir de** + day marks the start: **a partir del lunes**.
b4.e0.texto: The library will open at nine.
b4.e1.texto: The neighbours will read in the new room.
b4.e2.texto: The opening hours will change on Monday.
b5.f0.texto: The neighbourhood library shines at the end of the quiet street.
b5.f1.texto: Its tall windows let out a warm, yellow light.
b5.f2.texto: Inside, the long shelves smell of old paper.
b5.f3.texto: The neighbours walk unhurriedly among the wooden tables.
b5.f4.texto: A small girl carries a huge book with both hands.
b5.f5.texto: In the reading room, a big clock shows eight o'clock.
b5.f6.texto: A kind librarian switches off the lamps one by one.
b5.f7.texto: The students put their notebooks away in silence.
b5.f8.texto: At the door, the cold of the night touches their faces.
b5.f9.texto: Little by little, the street fills again with slow steps.
b6.o0.refuerzo: The titular goes at the top, not at the end.
b6.o1: la frase grande que resume la noticia
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! It gives the main idea in few words.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The author signs the news item, but that is not the titular.
b6.pregunta: What is the headline of a news item?
b7.frase: Mañana la biblioteca ____ a las nueve.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! The regular future: abrir + á.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Abrió» is past. «Mañana» asks for the future.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Abría» is imperfect, of a past habit.
b7.pregunta: Which form talks about the future?
b8.frase: La biblioteca ampliará su horario el lunes
b8.traduccion: The library will extend its opening hours on Monday
b9.o0.refuerzo: Four o'clock is two hours before, not after.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Seven o'clock is one hour later. It needs two.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Correct! Six plus two hours is eight.
b9.pregunta: It used to close at six. And two hours later?
b10.frase: A partir ____ lunes habrá más horas.
b10.o0.refuerzo: The article is missing: «de + el» joins as «del».
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «The library will open at nine».
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes! These are the working days, without the weekend.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is the weekend, exactly the opposite.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Holidays are another thing. «Entre semana» talks about working days.
p.amplía.consejo: From «ampliar». The tilde on «í» breaks the diphthong: «am-PLI-a».
p.partir.consejo: In «a partir de» it means «from». The stress is on «TIR».
p.próximo.consejo: The tilde on «ó» marks the stress. The «x» is «ks» and «c» before «i» is «k» here.
p.abrirá.consejo: Future of «abrir». The stress is on the last syllable, «RÁ».
p.cerrará.consejo: Future of «cerrar». The «c» before «e» is «th» in Spain.
p.leerán.consejo: Future of «leer». The two «e» vowels are in separate syllables.
p.cambiará.consejo: Future of «cambiar». The «b» and «v» sound alike in Spanish.
p.dejan.consejo: The «j» sounds like «h». The verb is «dejar», to let or to leave.
p.estantes.consejo: The stress is on «TAN». Think of shelves full of books.
p.guardan.consejo: «gua» is pronounced «gwa». The verb is «guardar», to keep or store.
p.resume.consejo: From «resumir». The stress is on «SU», and the «r» at the start is strong.
p.ampliará.consejo: Future of «ampliar». The stress is on the last syllable, «RÁ».
